newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Ayala Land sees no office glut.
newsitem.headline: Ayala Land sees no office glut.

text.p: The Philippine's largest property firm Ayala Land Inc said 15 percent of high-rise offices will be empty by 1999 but that does not necessarily mean a glut is in the offing, company president Francisco Licuanan III said on Thursday.

"Analysts said there will be 20 to 25 percent in 1998 but we feel vacancy rates will be about 15 percent at the worst and in 1999. We don't consider 15 percent a glut," Licuanan said. He added the oversupply may last up to the year 2001.
Luxury apartments, middle-income and industrial property markets will remain healthy, he added.
Strong demand is seen especially in the high-end condominium market, Licuanan added.
"The whole property sector is not in trouble. There will not be a collapse unless it is fed by emotions rather than logic," Licuanan told reporters.
There has been widespread concern that a proprty market slump may be on the cards in what some see as a repeat of the problems in Thailand.
Exposure of local banks to the property sector is less than those in Thailand and Licuanan said most local firms used pre-selling for finance.
Concerns of an oversupply in the property sector and the effect on banks have sent property and banking issues reeling the past few weeks.
"The whole hysteria is not justified and greatly exaggerated," Licuanan added.
